short_answer: Not for tuning. GuitarTuna's tuner is free, but only in standard tuning and with ads between uses; drop D, half step down and every other tuning sit behind a Tools subscription at about US$6.49 a month or US$29.99 a year. A microphone and some maths are all a tuner is, so the free tool here does chromatic tuning, a dozen instrument presets and a metronome in your browser with no ads and no account. If you want GuitarTuna's songs and lessons, that is a different product and a fair thing to pay for.
paywall:
GuitarTuna is the most downloaded tuner app and its business is subscriptions layered on top of a free tuner. The listing shows three tiers: Tools for custom and alternate tunings at about US$6.49 a month or US$29.99 a year, Play for the song and tab library at about US$9.99 a month or US$39.99 a year, and Learn for video lessons at about US$24.99 a month or US$139.99 a year. The free tier keeps standard tuning, the chord library and a basic metronome, with ads.

Reviews complain that features once free were moved behind the paywall over time, which is the pattern on every tool in this collection: the paid tier grows into the core action. Tuning to drop D is not a premium feature of a tuner. It is a different target frequency.
free_does:
• Chromatic tuning of any note, with a cents needle, the frequency, and a reference pitch you can set between 415 and 466 Hz.
  • Presets for guitar (standard, drop D, half step down), 4 and 5 string bass, ukulele, violin, viola, cello, mandolin and banjo. Tap a string to hear its reference tone.
  • A metronome scheduled on the audio clock, so it does not drift: 30 to 300 BPM, tap tempo, 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 5/4, 6/8 and 7/8, accented first beat, eighth, triplet and sixteenth subdivisions, and the tempo marking.
  • No ads, no account, nothing recorded. The microphone audio is analysed in your browser and discarded. Works offline after your first visit, so a rehearsal room with no signal is fine.
when_pay:
• You want to learn songs from tabs and chord sheets synced to the music. That library is GuitarTuna's real product and licensing it costs money.
  • You want structured video lessons with feedback.
  • You practise on your phone with the screen off and want the tuner and metronome as a native app with widgets. A browser tab needs to stay open.
